newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus prepares bill to lift interest rate ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus prepares bill to lift interest rate ceiling.

text.p: Cyprus authorities are preparing legislation to scrap the decades-old ceiling on interest rates before the island starts accession talks with the European Union, its finance minister said on Monday.
"It will be tabled to the House of Representatives for approval before the end of the year," Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told Reuters.
"Legislation is being drawn up now and it will be approved by the Council of Ministers before going to the House," he added.
A nine-percent interest rate level has been in force since 1944, imposed by the former British colonial administration to curb usury, limiting its use as an instrument of credit policy.
Cyprus, under increasing pressure to align its legislation with Europe, is pressing ahead with radical reforms to its economy before it starts accession talks with the bloc, scheduled for early 1998.
"The abolition of the interest rate ceiling is a crucial milestone in that direction," said Afxentis Afxentiou, governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus.
Earlier this year the central bank took the first step towards reform by creating a money market through regular treasury bill auctions under repurchase agreements.
"The financial system of Cyprus is in the process of radical liberalisation,' Afxentiou said.
Afxentiou was a guest speaker at an international bankers' conference organised by the Bank of Cyprus, aimed at promoting the island as a regional banking and offshore banking centre.
The two-day conference is an attempt to familiarise foreign bankers with the benefits of setting up a base in Cyprus, Bank of Cyprus chairman Solon Triantafyllides said.
"Cyprus has a very efficient banking sector which we are justifiably proud of," he said.
